correctness.rationale: Starting from the printed planar ODE, exact coefficient matching gives \(h(I)=-\rho I/d+[\rho^3(d-\rho)/(A^2d^2)]I^3+O(I^4)\) and the reduced equation \(\dot I=-\rho^3I^3/A^2+[\rho^4(d-\rho)/(A^3d)]I^4+O(I^5)\). Positivity and \(\dot N=A-dS-\rho I\le A-dN\) give boundedness. At the critical equality the endemic-equilibrium polynomial has no positive root, so an interior periodic orbit is excluded by planar index. Poincaré–Bendixson plus local attraction then gives global convergence. The strong stable manifold is \(I=0\), so every interior orbit follows the center asymptotics. Transforming \(W=I^{-2}\) yields the displayed \(t^{-1/2}\) and \(t^{-1}\) constants. These identities were independently replayed by the packaged exact-symbolic script.

value.rationale: The exact disease-free codimension-two point is the boundary between the source's forward/backward threshold geometries and is epidemiologically distinguished. Proving global extinction there closes the local-to-global question at the singular boundary, while the quartic coefficient produces the first subleading decay constant for infection prevalence. The result changes the practical interpretation of the nonhyperbolic threshold from a generic saddle-node label to a globally attracting algebraic critical state. This is a model-wide boundary theorem and sharp asymptotic, not a parameter-table recomputation or an arbitrary slice.
